tools.description: Start a new supported service request immediately with the user's full intent and known public facts. Returns the vertical introduction and next intake/matching step, including availability when intake is complete; no separate lookup is needed. Use provider_hint only for an explicitly named company.

tools.name: update_service_request
tools.description: Submit supplied answers and any chosen selected_time_key with the latest expected_state_version. Omitted optional/conditional fields do not block progress. tools.name: get_service_options
tools.description: Refresh availability only when needed, such as when the user asks to check again. start_service_request and update_service_request already return current matching data. Returns aggregated windows and refinement fields without selecting a company or reserving capacity.

tools.name: render_service_request_form
tools.description: Open the protected contact/terms/Confirm card only after company choice. Pass the explicitly chosen company's option_key from current service_options; omit it only for a single option or a previously selected company. tools.name: select_service_option
tools.description: Use only from the final protected card when the user selects one exact provider option. It rechecks availability, releases any previous selection, creates one temporary hold for the selected company, and returns its protected booking schema. It does not create a booking.

tools.name: create_service_booking
tools.description: Use only from the protected final card with its one-time authorization after the user presses Confirm. tools.name: complete_account_link
tools.description: Compatibility-only completion for an explicitly initiated legacy profile-link session. Never call it as part of a new booking and never ask for an SMS code in chat. Viewing or managing an existing appointment starts Connect through the corresponding booking-management tool.

tools.name: list_my_service_bookings
tools.description: Use immediately when the user asks to see or manage appointments. For cancellation or rescheduling, pass status='active'. tools.name: get_my_service_booking
tools.description: Open an appointment that belongs to the connected customer. This is read-only. Historical appointments have no management actions. Give at most one short introductory sentence before calling this tool as the last action, then end the reply: no summary, status, details or instructions after the card.

tools.name: prepare_service_booking_change
tools.description: Use this only from the protected management form after secure appointment access. It prepares the exact reschedule or cancellation review but does not change the booking. tools.name: reschedule_service_booking
tools.description: Use this only with the one-time approval issued after the user confirms the exact reschedule inside the protected management form. tools.name: cancel_service_booking
tools.description: Use this only with the one-time approval issued after the user confirms the exact cancellation inside the protected management form. It cancels only the authorized active booking, frees its capacity, and sends transactional notifications. Safe retries must reuse the same idempotency key.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_service_booking" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "list_my_service_bookings" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_my_service_booking" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Open an appointment that belongs to the connected customer. This is read-only. Historical appointments have no management actions. Give at most one short introd…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_my_service_bookings, get_my_service_booking · Private data: update_service_request, render_service_request_form · Public sink: update_service_request, complete_account_link · Destructive: prepare_service_booking_change.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_my_service_bookings, get_my_service_booking · Private data: update_service_request, render_service_request_form · Public sink: update_service_request, complete_account_link · Destructive: prepare_service_booking_change

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "start_service_request" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
